extracted.intended_audience: researchers and organizations seeking philanthropic research funding from Schmidt Sciences
extracted.subtask_description: Information for prospective grantees about how Schmidt Sciences organizes funding, what thematic centers it supports, and how to find/apply to current open calls. Emphasizes that funding is by solicited programs/RFPs rather than unsolicited proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unsolicited proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: We proactively seek out grant opportunities and do not accept unsolicited proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should not send unsolicited proposals; instead, consult and apply to the current open calls / RFPs listed on the site (links labeled 'Apply').

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding organized by centers and tailored programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Within each of our five centers, we organize scientific support through programs and projects—tailored to the needs of each specific hypothesis or challenge. Our team supports researchers pursuing hypotheses that address everything from basic-science questions to pressing problems facing the planet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is delivered via center-specific programs and projects that are tailored to particular hypotheses or challenges; applicants should align proposals to a center's program priorities and demonstrate fit with the specific hypothesis/challenge the program targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority research areas (center alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization focuses on five centers: AI & Advanced Computing; Astrophysics & Space; Biosciences; Climate; Science Systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each center has a thematic mission (e.g., 'AI & Advanced Computing — Supporting AI research and tools to accelerate breakthroughs across fields'; 'Astrophysics & Space — Unveiling the mysteries of the Universe with rapid realizations of innovative technology'; 'Biosciences — Harnessing biology's infinite possibilities at its intersection with chemistry, physics, and engineering'; 'Climate — Supporting climate research to bend the carbon curve and secure a sustainable future'; 'Science Systems — Breaking down barriers to scientific discovery by supporting people, tools, and communities'). Applicants should target opportunities that clearly map to one of these centers and the center's stated goals.
